name_reason: Compliant with global naming: data_fd2_ prefix + battle domain (battle core table) + descriptor summon_spell_palette_r_table. The _r suffix denotes the VGA RED channel (a semantic R/G/B component shared by the sibling _g_table @ 0x52553 and _b_table @ 0x52557), NOT a Ghidra address residue. The _table suffix reflects the data type/role: a 4-entry per-summon lookup keyed by summon_idx = spell_id - 0x20. No hex address residue in the name (no tail equal to 0x5254F or any data address). The 4-entry dimension is a domain dimension (4 summon spells 0x20..0x23), carried by the semantics, not address noise. Verified: the same naming pattern is already documented and used for the adjacent g/b/sfx-bank sibling tables in btltab2.c, so the name is consistent with the established convention.
purpose: Per-summon VGA palette RED channel value for the summon-spell (zhao huan xi) cinematic; the first of three adjacent per-summon RGB tables (R @ 0x5254F / G @ 0x52553 / B @ 0x52557), immediately preceding the SFX-bank-index table @ 0x5255B. Supplies the target red component for the palette interpolation during the summon strobe and fade-in.
logic_summary: Holds 4 per-summon RED bytes LE-packed into one dword = 0x3535333F, i.e. {0x3F,0x33,0x35,0x35}, indexed by summon_idx = spell_id - 0x20: [0]0x20=0x3F, [1]0x21=0x33, [2]0x22=0x35, [3]0x23=0x35. Sole accessor fd2_execute_summon_spell_cast (@ 0x27FC9) loads the WHOLE dword into a stack-local at function entry (palette_R = global; the single xref is READ @ 0x27FDA) and then byte-indexes that LOCAL copy as *(byte*)(&palette_R + summon_idx) for each fd2_interpolate_palette_range_toward_color call in the strobe loop and the fade-in loop. Because the byte-index lives in the consumer operating on its local dword copy, the global itself is a scalar uint32 holding the 4 channel bytes (an array would decay to a pointer at the whole-dword copy and store the address instead of the bytes). This matches the current Ghidra datatype 'dword' (len 4).
datatype: const uint32 (dword, 4 bytes; Ghidra dtype dword len=4; 4 RED channel bytes LE-packed, NOT uint8[4])
element_semantics: The 4 LE-packed bytes are the per-summon VGA 6-bit RED channel values (each 0..0x3F), one per summon spell: byte0=0x3F (0x20 xi tian shi), byte1=0x33 (0x21 feng yao jing), byte2=0x35 (0x22 po huai shen), byte3=0x35 (0x23 an xie gui). The whole dword is copied out once and byte-indexed in the consumer by summon_idx.
comment_original_issue: src per-symbol comment block (btltab2.c lines 115-135) was already accurate, precise, and complete (purpose, the dword-copy-then-byte-index mechanism, the scalar-uint32-not-uint8[4] reasoning, const-ness, values, and the R/G/B/sfx sibling relationship).
